name: US National Weather Service: point forecast (New York)

frame.part: top of the page, no scrolling

capture_note: Requested from incident.archivist@: same address, 1280 x 1600 viewport, top of page. Until then the study page draws the callouts on an empty frame. No image is kept in git.
licence_for_showing_the_screenshot: US government work, public domain (third-party map tiles excepted): a screenshot may be shown.
summary: Plain and complete: observed conditions at a named station, a strip of periods, a sentence for each with its numbers, and a box that says what the forecast is, when it was made and until when it is valid, with the forecaster's discussion one click away. No hazard was in force.

callouts.title: Observed now, at a named station
callouts.does_well: "Current conditions at New York City, Central Park (KNYC)", with coordinates, and "Last update 10 Nov 8:51 pm EST": an observation is tied to its station and time.

callouts.title: Nine periods in a strip
callouts.does_well: Day and night as separate periods; the chance of rain printed on the picture; high or low; two or three words.

callouts.title: A sentence per period, with numbers
callouts.does_well: "Rain. High near 59. East wind 9 to 11 mph. Chance of precipitation is 100%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible." Ranges, not single values.
callouts.fed_by: IPMA's descriptive forecast and warning texts (text_pt in warnings.json), quoted

callouts.title: About this forecast
callouts.does_well: The point, "Last Update", "Forecast Valid" from and to, and the data as KML and XML: provenance in a box of its own.

callouts.title: The forecast discussion
callouts.does_well: A link to the forecasters' own reasoning, in text, for this office.
